passages.provision_quote: On receipt of a report of the existence of a homeless encampment, a city or town shall notify the owner to remove the owner's tent, structure or other personal property from the area in which the encampment is located. If removal does not occur within twenty-four hours after the order to remove the property, the city or town shall claim the property and retain the property for a period of fourteen days, during which the owner may claim the owner's property. Unclaimed property may be disposed of pursuant to title 44, chapter 3. THe city or town shall clean the area in which the encampment was located.
passages.note: Operative clause for cities/towns: a notice-and-removal process for public-property encampments, with property forfeiture after 24 hours, and no criminal penalty for camping on public property itself.
House Third Reading roll call shows Montenegro voted Y on final passage of SB 1413.

rows.reasoning: Montenegro voted Y on House Third Reading of SB 1413 (2023), a single-subject homeless-encampment-removal bill. Its operative clause requires a city or town to notify an encampment's owner to remove property, then claim and retain it if not removed within 24 hours, a graduated-warning and civil-penalty process on public property, matching rung 4 ('Prohibiting encampments on public property, enforced through graduated warnings and civil penalties') and excluding rung 3 (no shelter-bed condition or service-diverting citations is named) and rung 5 (the text imposes no criminal penalty for camping on public property itself, only property forfeiture; criminal trespass applies only on private property).
